steps.content: With the luminous beings guiding your path, the once terrifying darkness dissipates in their gentle light. You feel something warm pulling you gently, your body moving toward the surface as your mind finally breaks free from chaos, returning to clarity.
When you realize it, you find yourself before a familiar stone slate. Only a few luminous beings remain beside you, beckoning you forward. You know that just a few steps ahead lies the exit.
But you can't bring yourself to leave like this. Though the luminous creatures have been guiding you all the way, you still haven't seen Pylgia herself—your precious companion.
You refuse to accept such an unspoken farewell. Looking back, you see specks of white light marking your path, forming a faint trail. Could she be hiding at the other end?
After what feels like an eternity, you find her at the path's end—Pylgia, now covered in barnacles and appendages, hiding in the depths of the shadows.
She senses your presence. A brief glimmer of light flashes across her pale pupils, only to fade away instantly.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: ...Why are you here?
She remains shrouded in darkness, seemingly attempting to hide her long-mutated form.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Go back. Just follow the light to leave... Go back to everyone else.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: You have fulfilled your duty. There's... nothing left here worth staying for.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No.
You shake your head, taking several steps closer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're still here. How can I just leave?
She lifts her face, one so pale it borders on translucence, her bloodless lips slowly parting. After a long silence, however, only a few words slip out.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: But I've... become like this. Are you... not afraid?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm not.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I'm worried... You said you were still with me, that you hadn't left. But you never showed up again, not even when I reached the end of the path.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If I leave now, will I... never see you again?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sorry... I'm just being childish, I guess.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You all have your own paths, and your fates are already sealed. I just... I just can't accept it...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even though a hundred years have passed, you all have to face this cruel end again... and I... I can't do anything... I'm just a bystander, just... just a child you keep sacrificing your lives to save...
Pylgia remains still and listens to you in silence, not much different from her human days. This was how she used to listen to the voice from the Abyss.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: You mean... we... everyone in the expedition died?
You feel reluctant to answer, but your expression gives everything away.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Mmm... For humans, death is the farewell that's hardest of all, I understand.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: You're suffering because you can't save us, right?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Yes.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: But we were people from a century ago.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: We were never meant to live in your time.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Not even... you guys in the expedition?

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: To be honest, I've never fully grasped many of the thoughts humans have.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Civilization, duty, dignity... Choosing these won't change the laws of life.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: All life equally becomes part of the cycle—birth, predation, reproduction, sickness, death, and at last, becoming nourishment for other life.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No, not like that. You are all heroes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This shouldn't be the end for you, at least not here... dying in agony like this, being devoured, burned... And now even you've been taken by this cursed Abyss...

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Then, what do you think our end should be like?

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: The world outside is no different. When the disaster strikes, everyone must fight with all they have just to survive.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Some had already changed, even before joining the expedition or entering this death area.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You mean...

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Yes. From the very beginning, I could feel that I was different from others.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: I could understand the language of sea creatures and survive in storms and whirlpools. I know the sea even more than the fish.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: But I found it more and more difficult to understand my own "kind." I didn't know who I was... or how to live with them.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: When I became like this, the world looked different to me again.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: You see, it's not all bad. At least now, I can have a proper conversation with you.
You recall your initial encounter with Pylgia. Back then, she always maintained a distance from her companions, never initiating conversations.

Just as she says, only after being contaminated by Mania and losing her human side, she has at last unburdened herself of inner turmoil, capable of accepting her true self and expressing who she truly is.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But Mania... This power is twisted, different from naturally formed life...

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: It is different, indeed.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: No dead human should be able to talk to another soul after a hundred years, right?

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Perhaps humans after Nightfall are changed by what you call... Mania, and have found a new path of evolution. They may have broken free from natural forces and entered a broader, unknown cycle of life.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Whether it is me or the other members of the expedition, we make our choice by our own will, becoming the next form of life.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Our consciousness hasn't faded—we're still doing what we find meaningful... From this perspective, we never truly die.
Pylgia gazes into the distance, her pale eyes gleaming with light.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Like me, they have been here all along, hoping to be your strength rather than a source of guilt, given our destined parting...

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: That, I believe, must be the meaning behind our reunion.
With Pylgia's words, you close your eyes as memories of all the encounters surge forth.

While sifting through these fleeting encounters for their faces, you finally understand that the memories need not be painful—what fills them are mostly moments that have captured their gentlest, most beautiful sides, not death, nor parting.

Perhaps they never truly left, lingering deep within your soul all along. At that moment, you feel an immense weight lifting from your heart. At last, you are freed from the anguish of their recurring deaths.
Pylgia smiles gently.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: No need for thanks. We're companions.
Your heart has returned to peace. Looking up, you see a blue light flickering in the distance—probably Schorl reminding you to go back.

That consists of your mission: the Abyss within the DisSea, the presence at its depths, the intelligence on spirit and substance, the hypotheses on human transformation... and above all, the story of the expedition.
You must bring them all back to reality.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: Let's take the submarine back. It carries the findings everyone fought so hard for.
Without you needing to say a word, Pylgia already catches your mind.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: It's time. I'll see you off.
In a shared comprehension, neither of you utters another word. You both harbor the same wish—that this farewell could wait just a little longer.
